text:
Ryan McLeod was one of Buffalo's better stories last season: 54 points, and Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.9 wins above replacement, 58th among 401 forwards. This season he has 1 goal and 4 points in 20 games, even as the Buffalo News notes he is closing in on an NHL milestone.

Most of the drop sits around him rather than in his game. The Sabres have scored 10.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own shooting is at 5.9% against a sustainable rate near 13.4%. That usually swings back. He is still playing the way Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked last season, carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries and setting up teammates, and his top speed ranks in the 97th percentile. One honest caveat from Evolving-Hockey: his 2025-26 results ran ahead of his chances, so last year's line overstates the baseline a little. Our numbers project about 31 points. Watch his minutes, which fell to 10.4 in his last game.
headline: Ryan McLeod's quiet start is mostly bad luck
